# Optimization and Cost Models
## Overview
This family encompasses techniques that optimize the computational cost of ray-grid traversal and determine optimal data structure parameters for volume rendering [G]. It addresses the bottleneck of redundant voxel or primitive evaluations along a ray by focusing on execution efficiency and resolution tuning rather than defining new traversal algorithms [G]. Unlike sibling methods that specify traversal order or coherence exploitation, this family optimizes the cost of executing traversal and the parameters under which it runs [G].
## Shared principles
All methods in this family build on [Ray-grid traversal](17-ray-grid-traversal.md), which advances analytically from one cell boundary to the next [G]. The core mechanism determines the next cell by comparing distances to upcoming boundaries on the x, y, and z axes, selecting the minimum distance to advance [G]. Optimization and cost models do not alter this fundamental geometric logic but instead optimize the *cost* of executing it or the *parameters* (like grid resolution) under which it runs [G].
## Subtopics

### [Ray Marching Optimization](10233-ray-marching-optimization.md)
Reduces the computational cost of evaluating participating media during ray traversal, distinct from spatial acceleration structures that skip empty space [G]. Chosen when material evaluation dominates traversal time.

### [Hardware-Specific Optimization](10277-hardware-specific-optimization.md)
Adapts volume rendering algorithms to exploit architectural characteristics of the target execution platform (CPU, GPU, TPU, or specialized accelerators) to maximize throughput and minimize latency [G]. Chosen when generic implementations fail to utilize hardware parallelism or cache hierarchies.

### [Grid Resolution Cost Model](12776-grid-resolution-cost-model.md)
Determines the optimal subdivision factor $m$ for a uniform grid by minimizing the average ray traversal time. Chosen for uniform grids where the trade-off between traversal steps and intersection checks requires analytical balancing.

### [Image-based Rendering Cost Model](17116-image-based-rendering-cost-model.md)
Estimates the latency and bandwidth requirements of remote visualization systems by optimizing the trade-off between parallel computational cost and network transmission overhead. Chosen for client-server architectures transmitting depth images or mesh geometry.

### [Uniform Subsampling Cost Model](17119-uniform-subsampling-cost-model.md)
Estimates the total latency for remote visualization tasks by optimizing the subsampling rate on a fixed uniform grid topology. Chosen when reducing dataset size via uniform grid reduction is preferred over multiresolution structures.

### [Workload-Centric Analysis Framework](18712-workload-centric-analysis-framework.md)
Connects individual optimizations with their system effects by tracing the forward rendering path through five specific counts: $N_{resident}$, $N_{active}$, $N_{pair}$, $N_{eval}$, and $N_{blend}$ [G]. Chosen for analyzing the systemic impact of combined optimization techniques.
